lane_impact: ui-hud lane: corrects this pass's claim ui-hud/transition-durations-exact, which asserts 17 frames for both shutters. A rebuild that ports 708 ms to the open shutter will be 41.7 ms slow on every room entry, node explore, teleport and rest - i.e. on essentially every world-exploration transition. Also invalidates the stated derivation (n-2)(n-1); the correct displacement law is n(n-1).
quote: `else if(this.transitionType == TRANSITION_BLACKOPEN){ this.blackup.y -= this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackdown.y += this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackMovtSpeed += 2; if(this.blackup.y <= -240){ this.blackup.y = -240; this.blackdown.y = 480; ... this.doAction(); } }` - no `counter` test anywhere in the branch. From startOpen (`blackup.y = 0; blackMovtSpeed = 0; counter = 0;`) displacement after n frames is n(n-1), so n=16 gives exactly 240 and the branch fires at frame 16. Simulation output: 'OPEN done at frame 16 y -240.0' vs 'CLOSE done at frame 17'.
text: The two black shutters are NOT symmetric: the closing shutter runs 17 frames (708 ms) because of an explicit counter gate, but the opening shutter has no gate and completes in 16 frames (667 ms).

lane_impact: Cross-lane measuring convention. Any lane converting a frame Y with 2.270 is 1 % wrong — this lane's own claim 7 did exactly that and published (639.4, 446.0) against a code truth of (640, 450). The lane journal already states the correct rule at docs/gauntlet/L0/systems/ui-hud.md:31-32; the structured claim contradicted it.
quote: `newScale = stageMC.stageHeight / originalHeight; offsetX = (stageMC.stageWidth - originalWidth * newScale) / 2; offsetY = 0; fitWidth = false;` — the wide-container branch fits HEIGHT and pillarboxes. At 1080 px that is exactly 1080/480 = 2.250 vertical; the measured horizontal is 1816/800 = 2.270, a ~0.9 % stretch introduced by the re-encode (a true 2.250 fit would give 1800 px of content, not 1816).
text: The reference video's frame-to-stage mapping is anisotropic — x divides by 2.270 but y divides by 2.250 — and the fit branch in the shipped code explains exactly why.

Against BattleUI.as:133 `skillSlotButton.x = 760 - i * 60;` (i=2,1,0) the least-squares fit with x0 fixed at the measured pillarbox edge 52 gives scale 2.2689 and residuals -0.35 / +0.30 / +0.10 px. Flash scales uniformly here (GameEngine.resizeHandler applies one newScale to both axes), so frame_y = -5.0 + 2.2689 * game_y; the capture crops ~5 px off the top and ~4 px off the bottom because 480 * 2.2689 = 1089 px > 1080.
text: The frame-to-game transform for video B is now pinned: game stage 800x480 rendered at scale 2.2689 with origin (52, -5.0) in frame pixels, fitted on three code-known slot centres with sub-0.4 px residuals.
